result.title: Preface
result.summary: The text introduces the State of Hawaii Employees’ Retirement System (ERS) Request for Proposals 2022-06 for a Real Assets Investment Consultant, issued October 3, 2022, and says potential offerors must register to receive addenda. It outlines the RFP’s sections: administrative and procurement rules; proposal submission requirements and confidentiality; evaluation stages, including mandatory screening, priority listing, interviews, best-and-final offers, final review, and award; scope of work, agreement period, compensation, and authorization; minimum qualifications, questions, fee proposal, and sample contract. The material is restricted to authorized recipients for responding to the RFP. ERS is a Hawaii public-employee defined-benefit system with over 74,000 active/inactive vested members and 45,000 retirees and beneficiaries. Its portfolio exceeded $22.5 billion at year-end 2021 and spans multiple asset classes, including real assets. ERS seeks a dedicated, non-discretionary consultant to assess real-assets managers and the program, covering real estate, timber, infrastructure, agriculture/farmland, and other real assets.

result.title: Hawaii ERS Background and Investment Overview
result.summary: Hawaii’s Employees’ Retirement System (ERS), established under state law, provides retirement benefits through contributory and non-contributory defined-benefit programs for more than 74,000 active and vested members and 45,000 retirees and beneficiaries across five state and county employer groups. It is governed by a Board of Trustees, with some administrative control held by the Department of Budget and Finance. As of December 31, 2021, its portfolio exceeded $22.5 billion and was managed by more than 54 firms across public equities and fixed income, real assets, mortgage loans, and alternative investments. The 2014 risk-allocation framework targets 65% Broad Growth, 35% Diversifying Strategies, and 0% Other, with allocations expected to be achieved by 2022. Investment policies and procedures and annual financial reports are available on the ERS website.

result.title: II. Purpose
result.summary: ERS seeks proposals for a dedicated non-discretionary consultant to assess its real assets program and managers, covering real estate and assets such as timber, infrastructure, and agriculture/farmland. Offerors should succinctly explain their distinctive value and identify services they cannot provide. RFP information is restricted to authorized use for proposal preparation and may not be generally distributed. The RFP is issued under Hawaii Revised Statutes Chapters 88 and 103D and related rules; offerors are presumed to know these requirements, and submitting a valid proposal represents that knowledge. Using the Chapter 103D RFP process does not waive applicable exemptions or trigger other Chapter 103D provisions. ERS Executive Director Thomas Williams is the Procurement Officer and Contract Administrator; contact details are provided. Timetable: RFP available October 3, 2022; questions due October 25 at 4:30 p.m. HST; ERS responses November 4; proposals due November 30 at 4:30 p.m. Dates are estimates and may change by addendum.

result.title: V. Procurement Timetable
result.summary: The procurement timetable lists the RFP release (October 3, 2022); deadline for questions (October 25, 4:30 p.m. HST); ERS responses (November 4); proposal deadline (November 30, 4:30 p.m. HST); priority-list determination (December 1–9); optional ERS facility visits (February 14–17, 2023); best and final offers (February 24, 4:30 p.m. HST); oral presentations (March 13–17); and contractor selection and award (April 10). result.title: VI. Communications with ERS; Questions
result.summary: Offerors and prospective offerors, including their agents, must not contact ERS trustees or staff about the RFP. Firms currently doing business with ERS may contact them only about that existing business, not the RFP. RFP information requests must be submitted in writing, including by fax or email, to the Procurement Officer, who is the sole contact from RFP release through awardee selection. Questions are accepted until 4:30 p.m. Hawaii Standard Time on October 25, 2022; ERS will answer in writing through the addendum process described in Paragraph XIII.

result.title: VII. Submission of Proposals
key_items: No faxed or e-mailed proposals will be considered or accepted.
result.summary: Offerors must review the solicitation, amendments, forms, and applicable requirements; submitting a proposal represents that they have carefully examined and understand the work and requirements. Each qualified offeror may submit one proposal only; alternatives are not accepted. By 4:30 p.m. Hawaii Standard Time on November 30, 2022, ERS must receive one unbound hard copy marked “original,” with sectional dividers, and one unencrypted electronic copy on USB. Label the proposal “Employees’ Retirement System of the State of Hawaii Real Assets Investment Consultant RFP 2202-06,” and address the sealed package to the Procurement Officer identified in Paragraph IV. Mark the package exterior with the ERS Real Assets Investment Consultant proposal title, RFP 2022-06, and firm name. Faxed and emailed proposals are not accepted. RFP information is restricted to authorized persons and use for responding to the RFP, not general distribution; all rights reserved 2017.

result.title: VIII. Receipt, Opening and Recording of Proposals; Late Proposals
result.summary: Proposals and modifications are time-stamped and securely held until the deadline. Before then, offerors may modify by written or fax notice with the sealed modification, or withdraw by written or fax notice; proposals may be withdrawn and resubmitted only before the final submission date. Proposals are opened privately by at least two procurement officials and shared only with personnel having a legitimate interest. A post-deadline register lists offerors and modification counts and becomes publicly inspectable only after award. Late submissions, modifications, and withdrawals are generally rejected, except when ERS personnel caused the delay; late withdrawal requests receive reasons for rejection. Priority-listed offerors may submit best and final offers. Mistakes cannot be corrected after award. Before award, the Procurement Officer may seek confirmation; alleged mistakes may allow correction or withdrawal. During discussions or before the best-and-final deadline, priority-listed offerors may modify or withdraw freely. Otherwise, clearly evidenced intended offers are corrected without withdrawal; qualifying material mistakes may permit withdrawal. ERS may waive or allow cures for minor informalities and conduct discussions as needed.

result.summary:

result.title: XII. Disqualification of Proposals
result.summary: ERS may reject proposals that fail RFP requirements or show inadequate understanding, or that contain conflicting terms. Grounds for disqualification include collusion, poor past responsibility or cooperation, legal noncompliance, conditional or ambiguous submissions, prohibited reservation clauses, lateness, State contract arrears or defaults, insufficient experience, and conflicts of interest or impaired independence. ERS may amend the RFP before the response deadline through consecutively numbered addenda, including to answer inquiries. It may cancel the RFP or reject proposals in whole or part when in its best interests, and may modify an agreement to address circumstances beyond its control affecting service delivery. No bid, performance, or payment bonds are required. Proposal acceptance follows the procurement timetable; the offeror must be capable of performance, as judged solely by ERS, and the successful offeror will receive written notice of award. ERS may award based on written responses received, without prior… (the text ends mid-sentence).

result.title: XVII. Acceptance of Proposal and Execution of Contract
result.summary: Acceptance will follow the Procurement Timetable. The offeror must be capable of performing the RFP and contract requirements, as determined solely by ERS; the successful offeror will receive written award notice. ERS may award based on written submissions without prior discussions. Attachment A’s terms are deemed accepted unless objections and alternative language are submitted; ERS may negotiate further. The contract comprises the RFP and amendments plus negotiated terms. The selected offeror must sign and return the contract within ten days of receipt, unless granted more time; it binds ERS only when properly executed by all parties. If the awardee fails to contract on time, ERS may consider the next-ranked offeror or seek new proposals in its best interests. The document also restricts its use to authorized persons responding to the RFP and prohibits general distribution.

result.title: XVIII. Debriefing
result.summary: Nonselected offerors may request a debriefing in writing from the Procurement Officer or designee within three working days of contract award posting. If requested by multiple offerors, a combined debriefing will be held, to the extent practicable within seven working days of the first request. ERS decides whether it is conducted in person or by telephone. The stated location is the Employees’ Retirement System of the State of Hawaii, City Financial Tower, 201 Merchant Street, Suite 1400, Honolulu, HI 96813. Any protest after a debriefing must be filed within five working days under HAR §103D-303(h).

result.title: XIX. Requirements for Doing Business in the State of Hawaii
result.summary: Before contract award, the successful offeror must show compliance with Hawaii laws on general excise tax, unemployment insurance, workers’ compensation, temporary disability insurance, and prepaid health care, and be incorporated/organized in Hawaii or registered to do business there. A Hawaii Compliance Express Certificate of Vendor Compliance can document current status and is accepted for contracting and final payment. Untimely proof may prevent award. Contractors must remain compliant throughout the contract, including extensions; ERS may check status and withhold payments if it is not compliant or has expired, without this constituting breach, excusing performance, or entitling the contractor to interest. The RFP proposal must describe qualifications, availability, and fees, and include a cover letter, questionnaire answers, ADV Parts 1 and 2, ethics code, references, fee proposal, sample reports, financial statement, and minimum-qualifications certification. The cover letter to the Procurement Officer must provide contact details, confirm acceptance of RFP terms, acknowledge all amendments/addenda, and identify the offeror’s legal form.

result.title: III. Confidential or Proprietary Information
result.summary: Offerors must clearly identify and separate trade secrets or proprietary information they seek to keep confidential; public-inspection requests are governed by Hawaii law, and neither the entire proposal nor the fee proposal may be confidential. RFP information is restricted to authorized ERS recipients and use in responding to this RFP, not general distribution. ERS seeks a fair, competitive selection of a high-quality investment consultant but retains discretion not to select the lowest-cost offeror or make an award. A Procurement Officer-selected committee will evaluate timely proposals in six phases: minimum qualifications and mandatory requirements; priority-list establishment; optional facility inspections; interviews; final evaluation; and award. Criteria in specified RFP sections will be used to evaluate and rank proposals, and ERS may modify criteria or other RFP provisions before final submissions. Phase 1 uses a pass/no-pass review to assess responsiveness; failure to meet minimum qualifications or mandatory requirements may result in disqualification.

result.title: Real Assets Consultant Proposal Evaluation
result.summary: The Employees’ Retirement System of the State of Hawaii seeks a high-quality investment consultant through a fair, competitive process and retains sole discretion over contract awards. It may select an offeror other than the lowest-cost bidder or make no award. A committee appointed by the Procurement Officer will evaluate proposals submitted by the RFP deadline in six phases: review of minimum qualifications and mandatory requirements; creation of a priority list; optional facilities inspections; interviews with priority-listed offerors; final proposal evaluation; and contract award.

result.title: III. Evaluation Criteria
key_items: IV. Phase 1 – Evaluation of Minimum Qualifications and Mandatory Requirements
result.summary: Evaluation criteria in Sections V and VII will rank proposals; ERS may revise the criteria or other RFP terms before final responses are due. Phase 1 assesses minimum qualifications and mandatory submissions on a pass/no-pass basis to determine responsiveness. Proposals failing may be rejected as nonresponsive; only those passing proceed to Phase 2. Offerors must be registered investment advisers, have at least three years of real-assets consulting experience, serve at least one public defined-benefit retirement system with over $5 billion in assets, be based and subject to service of process in the U.S., and assign a primary consultant with at least seven years’ domestic and international real-assets consulting experience for public pension plans. Required submissions are a cover letter, questionnaire answers, Form ADV Parts 1 and 2, code of ethics, references, fee proposal, sample reports, financial statement, and minimum-qualifications certification. The RFP information is restricted to authorized users for proposal preparation and is not for general distribution.

result.title: V. Phase 2 – Establishment of Priority List of Offerors
result.summary: Phase 2 classifies offerors passing minimum qualifications and mandatory requirements as acceptable or potentially acceptable. If more than three qualify, the Evaluation Committee evaluates all proposals and ranks the top three. Criteria are weighted: consulting experience, organizational stability, personnel and deliverables (45 points); institutional-community presence, client and investment-vehicle experience, and strategy capabilities (35); ongoing manager and market information (20); fees (0), for 100 total. In Phase 3, ERS may inspect facilities February 14–17, 2023, or by arrangement, and the Board may interview priority-listed offerors in Honolulu during March 13–17. Phase 4 best and final offers are due to the Procurement Officer by 4:30 p.m. HST February 24, 2023; otherwise, the prior offer stands as final. Phase 5 introduces ERS’s final evaluation of priority-listed proposals under criteria not included in the excerpt. The document also restricts its use to authorized RFP respondents and prohibits general distribution.

VII. Phase 4 – Best and Final Offers
result.summary: Evaluation totals 100 points: 45 for consulting experience, organizational stability, personnel, and delivery capabilities; 35 for institutional real-assets experience and strategy expertise; 20 for current manager and market information; and 0 for fees. In Phase 3, the ERS Board may interview priority-listed offerors in Honolulu during March 13–17, 2023, and inspect their facilities February 14–17 or by convenient arrangement. In Phase 4, best and final offers are due to the Procurement Officer by 4:30 p.m. HST on February 24, 2023; if none is received, the offeror’s previous offer becomes its best and final offer.

result.title: VIII. Phase 5 - Final Evaluation of Proposals
result.summary: In Phase 5, ERS will make final evaluations of priority-listed offerors’ proposals using a 100-point scale: experience and approach to investment policy and long-term planning, understanding of real-assets markets and strategies (30); leadership, management, organizational strength, and key personnel (25); investment philosophy and process, resources, and approach to manager searches and performance measurement/presentation (20); client references (5); and fees (20). Fee points are calculated as the lowest proposal fee multiplied by 12.0 for the first three years, or 8.0 for six years, divided by the fee being evaluated. The document also restricts the information to authorized ERS recipients for responding to the RFP, prohibits broader distribution, and reserves all rights (2017).

result.title: IX. Phase 6 – Award
result.summary: The ERS Board of Trustees makes the final award selection. RFP information is restricted to authorized users and use in responding to the RFP. The contract seeks comprehensive, non-discretionary pension investment consulting for ERS; the contractor must be an investment adviser registered under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and enter an agreement substantially in the form of Attachment A. The initial term is approximately July 1, 2023–June 30, 2026, with an ERS-option three-year extension through June 30, 2029. ERS may also extend the agreement at no cost to finish manager searches underway. Final payment follows receipt of the final quarterly performance report and other required materials. The annual fixed fee is paid quarterly, with monthly work statements; work outside that fee is billed upon completion. Statements must describe work in enough detail to support payment, which ERS processes under its standard procedures.

result.title: ERS Investment Consulting Scope and Agreement Period
result.summary: The Hawaii Employees’ Retirement System seeks comprehensive, nondiscretionary pension fund investment consulting services through this RFP. The contractor must be an investment adviser registered under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and provide the services described in the RFP under an agreement substantially in the form of Attachment A. The agreement is expected to begin around July 1, 2023, and run for approximately three years, ending June 30, 2026, unless terminated earlier. ERS may grant a three-year extension, deciding in 2026; if granted, the agreement ends June 30, 2029. Final payment follows receipt of the expiring year’s June 30 quarterly performance report and other required materials. ERS may also extend the agreement, at no additional cost, solely to complete investment manager searches underway at the end of the existing term.

result.title: III. Compensation
result.summary: The annual fixed fee is paid quarterly, with monthly statements; other work is billed upon completion. Statements must detail work sufficiently to justify payment, and ERS processes claims under its procedures. Payments beyond the current fiscal year depend on available appropriations, with no liability until funds are provided. This is a multi-term contract with a consistent annual fee unless adjustments are allowed; continuation depends on funding, with timely notice if funds are unavailable. Offerors must price the full term, and cancellation may require reimbursement of applicable unamortized, reasonably incurred nonrecurring costs, without affecting termination rights. The ERS Chief Investment Officer is the contractor’s liaison, chairs status meetings, coordinates scheduling, and monitors performance. Work requires ERS approval; unauthorized work is at the contractor’s risk. The contractor may not bind ERS beyond the contract period and must follow ERS policies. The CIO coordinates consultant activities under Investment Committee direction, implementing decisions and overseeing managers. Consultant coverage includes all real assets, including real estate, timber, infrastructure, and agriculture/farmland, under the all-inclusive flat fee; specific duties follow. The document is restricted to authorized RFP use and not for general distribution.

result.title: Multi-Term Contract and Contractor Oversight
key_items: V. Liaison and Authorization to Proceed
result.summary: Funds are not currently available beyond the fiscal year, and ERS has no payment obligation for later performance until funds are made available. The multi-term contract keeps the annual fixed fee constant unless an authorized adjustment applies; it may be cancelled if future-period funding is unavailable, without affecting termination rights. The purchasing agency head must notify the contractor promptly of funding unavailability, offerors must price the full performance term, and eligible unamortized nonrecurring costs will be reimbursed upon cancellation. The ERS Chief Investment Officer is the primary liaison, chairs status meetings, helps schedule, and monitors performance. Work undertaken before ERS approval to proceed is at the contractor’s risk, and ERS is not bound by it.

result.title: VI. Scope of Services
result.summary: The consultant may not commit ERS beyond the contract term and must follow ERS policies; the CIO coordinates its work under Investment Committee direction and oversees implementation and managers. The all-inclusive flat fee covers all real assets, including real estate, timber, infrastructure, agriculture, commodities, and opportunistic assets. Duties include developing and reviewing five-year and annual strategic and pacing plans, objectives, policies, benchmarks, portfolio construction, policy updates, ESG analysis, and market research; setting manager criteria and reviewing annual manager plans, budgets, properties, acquisitions, and dispositions. The consultant will source and conduct due diligence on managers and investment vehicles, support negotiations and Board recommendations, and monitor managers against benchmarks and plan requirements. It will report quarterly on portfolio and manager performance and markets, including property returns; assist with capital calls, distributions, LPAC matters, and manager consent or voting requests; attend up to eight annual meetings and annual portfolio reviews; and educate staff and the Board. It must provide audit access, perform consistent related duties, and integrate financially relevant ESG factors, assess risks and opportunities, and conduct requested ESG research.

result.title: MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS CERTIFICATION
result.summary: The Offeror certifies to the Employees’ Retirement System that it is registered under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940; has at least three years’ experience as a real-assets investment consultant, with commencement dates requested for each proposal area; serves at least one public defined-benefit retirement system client with more than $5 billion in assets, with client names requested; and assigns a primary consultant with at least seven years’ domestic and international investment consulting experience for public pension plans, with the consultant’s name and experience requested. It also certifies that its principal place of business is in the United States and it is subject to U.S. service of process, with its location requested, and that, if awarded the contract, it will act as a fiduciary to ERS.

It also asks about essential policy-development issues; for ERS, real-asset risk categories and supporting real-return assumptions, inflation outlook and investment recommendations, strategies to achieve risk-adjusted returns, and whether a 5% minimum total real return over the next five to ten years is appropriate. Further topics are portfolio leverage reporting, program-level risk-management tools, and the firm’s ESG policy. The material is restricted to authorized ERS recipients for responding to the RFP and not for general distribution.

It requests benchmark customization methods and resources, sample standard and IMA quarterly reports, report availability and executive summaries. It also asks how investment-advisor problems are identified and corrected, actions taken for poorly performing commingled funds and separate accounts or direct investments, and quantitative ESG measures. result.summary: The Deal Review section requests information on the firm’s experience preparing due diligence reviews for new acquisitions and existing properties, managing client appraisals, and writing appraisal reviews, with sample materials requested for Appendix D. It asks about work with institutional owners, advisers, and lenders on workout or problem properties and examples of value added; policies for allocating real estate investments among clients, with the policy attached in Appendix E if available; experience reviewing and recommending deals across Europe, Far East/Asia/Australia, Latin America, the Middle East, and other regions, plus a five-year investment outlook; and experience with timber, infrastructure, agriculture/farmland, and other alternative real assets, including recommended allocation ranges for a public pension such as Hawaii ERS and whether, how much, and why that allocation might grow. The material is restricted to authorized ERS recipients and use in responding to the RFP, and may not be generally distributed.

result.title: FEE PROPOSAL
result.summary: The fee proposal must remain valid for at least six years from the contract’s effective date, covering an expected three-year term and a possible three-year ERS extension. Fees should reflect the services in Paragraph VI of the Scope of Work and include travel, taxes, and all expenses. Offerors must quote all-inclusive annual flat fees for years 1–3 and, if extended, years 4–6, with subtotals for years 1–3 and total fees for years 1–6. Payment terms are in Paragraph III. The final contract fee is the consultant’s sole compensation; no other monetary or nonmonetary benefits may arise from the relationship.
